neighbours.label: the word pieces 'el' / 'ad' / 'al' ('els', 'ads') when they are their own token continuing a short word start (Eiff·el, F·ad·iman, op·al, e·els); not the same letters inside a whole-word token (chapel, canal, nomad)
fire: The postcard showed the Eiffel Tower lit up at midnight.
The necklace had a single opal set in silver.
Smoked eels are a speciality of the villages along that coast.
The anthology was introduced by Clifton Fadiman in a short preface.
The goalkeeper Ohad saved two penalties in the final.
The lawyer, Mr Awad, asked the court for more time.
The fund is run by IFAD together with local banks.
From the bridge you can see Eiffel's iron viaduct across the valley.
quiet: The postcard showed the Empire State Building lit up at midnight.
The necklace had a single pearl set in silver.
Smoked herring is a speciality of the villages along that coast.
The anthology was introduced by Conrad Aiken in a short preface.
The goalkeeper Rafael saved two penalties in the final.
The old chapel stood beside the canal near the hotel.
The nomad led his camel to the well and ate a salad.
From the bridge you can see the model railway and the metal gate.

notes: Early layer: tested as spelling pieces. Probes: Eiffel 0.89, opal 0.84, eels 0.80, Fadiman 0.82, 'Ohad, Ebel, Ifad, Ayad, Awad' 0.74; whole-token words with the same letters (nomad, chapel, camel, canal, Conrad, salad, Raphael) 0.00-0.13. Which word starts license the piece is not pinned down (Gilead 0.05).
